title: 49. Alterations in the proteome across subcutaneous adipose depots in finishing beef steers.
content:
Abstract
Subcutaneous adipose tissue is a key regulator of energy storage, endocrine signaling, and carcass composition in beef cattle. Despite its role in growth and metabolic regulation, subcutaneous adipose tissue is often treated as a homogeneous tissue, with limited consideration given to functional differences among anatomical depots. Therefore, the objective of this study was to characterize differences in the subcutaneous adipose proteome across anatomical sites in beef cattle. Three Angus steers (body weight = 534 ± 37 kg) were used to collect subcutaneous adipose biopsies from the rump, brisket, and ventral abdomen. Adipose tissue samples were flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored until further analysis. A discovery-based LC–MS/MS proteomics approach, coupled with bioinformatic analysis, was employed for protein profiling and quantitative assessment. In total, 791 protein groups were successfully identified and quantified across the three anatomical depots, of which 485 proteins were shared among all sites. The rump contained 90 unique proteins, the ventral abdomen contained 9 unique proteins, and the brisket contained 43 unique proteins. Additionally, 15 proteins were shared between the rump and ventral abdomen, 90 proteins were shared between the ventral abdomen and brisket, and 20 proteins were shared between the rump and brisket. Depot-specific differences were observed in the abundance of individual proteins, including greater abundance of NADH dehydrogenase–related proteins in the rump compared with the ventral abdomen and brisket, whereas IGFN1 was minimally detected in the rump relative to the other depots. Collectively, these results demonstrate that subcutaneous adipose tissue exhibits marked proteomic heterogeneity across anatomical locations, highlighting the importance of anatomical site when evaluating adipose tissue function, metabolic regulation, and its contribution to carcass composition in beef cattle.
